My Prometheus I suppose you [have already begun] printing before this letter reaches
you — [I am] somewhat doubtful about this said question of pr[oofs.] Who will revise
the press? If possible, & if there is time, I should be very glad that the printer could divide
the whole poem into two proofs & send it to me for the last corrections. — In this case
[it ought to be canc.] the proofs ought to be taken off on thin paper and sent to me by the
Post . . . If there is any difficulty in this, allow me to recommend you the utmost caution
in revising the press . . . of course I would pay whatever might be necessary for the revi-
sion . . . provided it were done correctly. — Mr. Hunt is [revising] Julian & Maddalo, but
I will not [burden] him with the Prometheus — [I am the] more anxious because I con-
